description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:152-156, 384-425

`SctVerifier<V>` does not document `Send + Sync` requirements on
`V: SignatureVerifier`. The struct itself is `Send + Sync` iff
`V: Send + Sync` (auto-derived).

Non-negotiable #6 says cache-friendly types must be `Send + Sync`.
The doc comment in non-negotiable #6 explicitly states this requirement
for "public result/error types" but the constraint extends to the
verifier types callers will share across threads.

Typical caller deployment:

- Trust state (log list + verifier) is constructed at startup
- Wrapped in `Arc<SctVerifier<DefaultVerifier>>`
- Shared across N async tasks, each receiving a connection,
  parsing SCTs, and calling `verify_*` concurrently

This works today because `DefaultVerifier` is `Copy + Send + Sync`,
`CtLogList` is `Send + Sync` (BTreeMap of plain data), and the
verify methods take `&self`. But the contract is not stated in any
doc comment. A caller reviewing whether they can wrap in `Arc` has
to inspect the trait bounds and auto-trait propagation themselves.

Recommendation: add a contract clause to `SctVerifier`'s doc
comment:

> `SctVerifier<V>` is `Send + Sync` whenever `V: SignatureVerifier`
> is, and the verify methods take `&self`, so the same verifier may
> be shared across threads behind `Arc` without locking.

Same clause belongs on `CtLogList`. Add a `static_assertions`-style
test that fails compilation if these are ever changed:

```rust
fn _assert_send_sync()
where
    SctVerifier<DefaultVerifier>: Send + Sync,
    CtLogList: Send + Sync,
{}
```

Priority P3 because the property holds today; this is making the
implicit explicit, which prevents accidental regression.
title: verify_embedded_scts Send/Sync contract unstated — common pattern is shared SctVerifier across worker threads
